# Auto-generated track: ELEMENT CATALOGUE, IMPORT PROCESS, DIVERSITY BACKLOG

Status: investigation shipped 2026-09-06 (this doc + two tools + one picker
change). No generator geometry was changed: every element listed in section 1
keeps its current emitter, knob and default.

Companion docs: `AUTOTRACK_HANDOVER.md` (what was pending after phase 1),
`AUTOTRACK_BRANCHES.md` (fork spec), `AUTOTRACK_STREAMING.md` (phase 2),
`AUTOTRACK_TRACK_CENSUS.md` (GENERATED by `re/tools/tg_track_census.py`: the
per-level numbers this doc quotes).

`TG:<line>` = `td5mod/src/td5re/td5_trackgen.c` as it was BEFORE the split, the
31134-line monolith at commit 2b9bc493 (`git show 2b9bc493:td5mod/src/td5re/td5_trackgen.c`).
The same day it was split into themed modules; `codemap/sections.tsv` gives the
live location of every banner. Module map (monolith line ranges in
`scripts/refactor/split_trackgen_plan.json`):

| Module | Holds |
|---|---|
| `td5_trackgen.c` | spec + knobs, RNG, page-slot layout, parallel groundwork, element accounting, rail ownership, time of day, centerline, elevation, bridge placement, range emitter, road mesh, side buffers, scenery three-phase driver, build / regenerate / stream entry points |
| `td5_tg_branch.c` | fork corridors, long diverging branch, carriageway query, branch pavement, avenue divider |
| `td5_tg_guard.c` | on-road geometry backstop, MESHTAG sidecar, pavement provenance, over-water and coast audits |
| `td5_tg_city.c` | bend-fold authority, facades, turn continuation, city pavement, run-end census, side-street occupancy, street furniture group A |
| `td5_tg_streets.c` | side-street direction and occupancy, intersections, parks and houses, real intersections, infill, measurement sweeps |
| `td5_tg_terrain.c` | trees, props, road surfaces, biomes and adjacency, snow, one-side sea, outskirts, topo authority, forest side roads, tree bands, ponds, ground chain |
| `td5_tg_bridge.c` | water, tunnel bore vs underpass, portals, overpass, run coalesce, structural tie, median end faces, bridge measurement harness |
| `td5_tg_furniture.c` | guardrails, start/finish gantry, curve direction signs |
| `td5_tg_pages.c` | every TEXTURES.DAT page emitter |
| `td5_trackgen_internal.h` | the shared private declarations (macros, types, cross-module prototypes and externs) |

---

## 1. What the generator emits today (classification)

Three layers. Only the first is track TOPOLOGY (what the car drives on and
what the AI, minimap and lap logic read); the other two are art.

### 1a. Strip topology (STRIP.DAT + LEFT/RIGHT.TRK)

| Element | Emitter | Knob | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| Section picker: straight / sweeping curve / acute (up to 88 deg per section) / "dual lane" (WIDER road, same lane count) | `tg_build_centerline` TG:2129, weights TG:29829 | `TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_PCT_STRAIGHT/CURVE/ACUTE/DUAL`, `CURVESAFE`, `SPANS` (1800), `LANES` (4, clamped 2..4) | ON |
| Elevation: sum of sines + macro relief, grade cap 0.120 | `tg_apply_elevation`, TG:2545 | `TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_ELEVATION` (6000), `GRADE` (120), `TD5RE_R8_SHAPE_RELIEF` | ON |
| Fork: split and rejoin (types 8 / 9 / 1 / 10 / 11), up to 4 per track, corridor widened, avenue divider, gore | fork loop TG:5471, `tg_append_row` 3052, rejoin TG:5603 | `TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_BRANCHES`, `BRANCH_MINLEN` (24), `BRANCH_GAIN`, `BRANCH_VARY_SEP`, `BRANCH_WIDEN` | ON |
| Long diverging branch (260 spans, bow 3.75 widths) | TG:3181 | `TD5RE_R8_SHAPE_LONGBRANCH` | OFF |
| Surface grip per biome (tarmac / gravel / dirt / ice / cobble), one code per span, alternate-surface mask fixed at 0x09 | `tg_surface_attr` TG:8330, `k_road_surf` TG:7557 | biome table | ON |

Single-valued today, and therefore the first diversity targets:

* **Lane count** is one number for the whole track (`lanes_here = spec->lanes`
  TG:2333) and the knob is clamped to 2..4 (TG:29841). The comment justifying
  the clamp, "shipped tracks only ever use 2-4 lanes", is wrong: see section 3.
* **Span types** emitted: 1 and 8..11 only. Shipped tracks use 2..7 on every
  lane change (section 4).
* **Branch shape** is one kind, a detour that bows out and rejoins. Shipped
  tracks are 126 parallel splits and 21 shortcuts out of 147 forks, and no
  detours (section 5).

### 1b. Scenery geometry (MODELS.DAT meshes, no collision)

Bridges (raised-cosine deck, rails, kerb, piers, water, coast), tunnel bore vs
city underpass (portal, lamps), overpass and crossing surround, median end
faces, side streets and "real intersections" (cross-street carriageway, side
walls, zebra, flank), forest side roads, turn continuation, city pavement +
kerb + verge band + fence + lamps + back rows, facades with storefront ground
floor and tower districts, fork-back plaza, parks and houses (OFF), gap-interior
infill, guardrails (armco / W-beam / stacked), water (sea plane, one-side sea
OFF, ponds), trees and tree-line bands, props (people, statues, animals, lamp
glow), TD6 street furniture (crate, bin, phone, bench, awning, bollard, plank),
start/finish gantries, direction signs, terrain slab / far band / hills / step
walls, snow ground. Every one is knob-gated; the per-emitter table with file
lines is in the survey that produced this doc and in `codemap/sections.tsv`
(search the `[R<n> ...]` banners).

Sources used so far: TD5 levels 001, 002, 003, 013, 014, 015, 018, 023. Never
mined: Bern 003 (beyond banners), Kyoto 004, Washington 005, Munich 006,
Edinburgh 016, Blue Ridge 017, Cheddar 025, Jarash 026, Courmayeur 027, Maui
028, Newcastle 029, Bez 037, Drag 039, and ALL eleven converted TD6 levels
(007..012, 018..022: 61..368 pages each, 2226 pages in total).

Biomes: CITY, FIELDS, FOREST, INDUSTRIAL, ALPINE, COAST, ORIENTAL, plus
snow-only ALPTOWN; 150-span cells; adjacency by climate and urbanity distance
of at most 1 and a per-biome repeat cap (TG:7632..7780). The section mix is
NOT biome-driven (TG:7576).

## 2. The import process (how a shipped element becomes a generator element)

Two paths exist today. Neither reaches the C generator at runtime: the
generator reads only FORWSKY.png from shipped levels (TG:2909) and bakes
everything else from headers.

1. **Textures (art) into the C generator**: pick pages, bake a header, reserve
   page slots in the `[R3] RESERVED PAGE SLOTS` chain (TG:163..562), add an
   emitter call in `tg_emit_textures`, reference the page from a mesh emitter.
2. **Geometry into a hand-built custom track**: `scripts/track_editor_mcp`
   (`import_track` for centerline / branches / checkpoints, `extract_prototype`
   + `place_prototype` for whole building meshes with their pages,
   `import_texture` per page). Output is `re/assets/levels/level04x`, not the
   generator.

What this change adds to path 1 (all read-only over assets, existing headers
are never rewritten):

* **`re/tools/gen_tg_pages.py MANIFEST.json`**: one JSON manifest of
  `[level, page, description]` per set produces a header with the exact
  `k_real_<set>_<name>...` symbol shape `tg_emit_r8var_*_pages` already
  consumes. No more one script per import round.
  `--list-mined` scans every `td5_tg_*.h` for its source-page comments (63
  pages today) and the importer refuses a page already baked unless
  `--allow-dup`, so the hand-copied `ALREADY` sets in the older scripts are no
  longer the guard.
* **Picker import handle**: in a dev build, the free-cam geometry picker on a
  SHIPPED track now copies `{"track":"level014","level":14,"page":276,...}`
  (it used to say `AUTO` for every track). `gen_tg_pages.py --from-pick
  MANIFEST SET` appends the pasted pick(s) to a manifest set. "I like that
  wall" is therefore: fly to it, click, paste, re-run the generator.
* **`re/tools/tg_track_census.py`**: the sweep in section 3..5, re-runnable
  after converting more TD6 levels (`--changes N` dumps the rows around every
  lane change in level N).

Still manual, in order of value:

1. Reserving the page slot + emitter call in `td5_trackgen.c` for a new set
   (about 15 lines per set; see `tg_emit_r8var_rail_pages` TG:29405).
2. Mesh prototypes (buildings, bridges, gantries) into the generator. The
   Python side already extracts them (`td5_scenery.py` / `extract_prototype`);
   the C side would need a baked mesh header or a runtime loader for a
   `re/assets/tg_protos/` directory. Not started.
3. The base header's missing script: rewrite `td5_tg_real_tex.h` from a
   manifest ONLY with a byte-identical check, or leave it (it is stable).

## 3. Census: what the shipped tracks actually use (TD5 + TD6)

From `AUTOTRACK_TRACK_CENSUS.md` (19 TD5 levels, 11 converted TD6 levels,
6 custom). Numbers per span on the main ring.

| Property | Shipped range | Generator today |
|---|---|---|
| Lane count | 2..10 per span; Washington is 6 and 8 only, Honolulu and Maui reach 10, TD6 Hong Kong reaches 9 | one value, 2..4, default 4 |
| Lane-count changes per track | 18 (Keswick) to 88 (Paris); 1348 in total, 1216 of them across a SHARED vertex row | 0 |
| Span types | 1..11 everywhere; 2..7 on lane changes | 1, 8, 9, 10, 11 |
| Surface codes | 1 (Sydney) to 45 distinct (London); TD5 uses 0x11 / 0x13 / 0x31 / 0x41 / 0x51 / 0xF1..0xFA, TD6 a 0..45 class index with its own grip table (`k_td6_surface_grip`) | 5 grip classes, low nibble only |
| Jump records (forks) | 0 (Keswick, SF, Bern, Kyoto, Washington, Munich, Cheddar, Jarash) to 28 (London); 147 in total | up to 4 |
| Texture pages per level | 40 (Tahoe) .. 520 (San Francisco) | about 85 |

The six TD5 point-to-point city tracks with ZERO forks (001..006) get their
variety entirely from lane changes, surfaces and scenery. The fork-heavy
tracks (London 28, Paris 21, Tokyo 17) are the city circuits.

## 4. Lane management: the primitive the generator is missing

Shipped tracks change lane count WITHOUT breaking the shared vertex row that
the generator depends on (`tg_emit_strip`). The mechanism is the span type:

| Type | `td5_types.h` name | Meaning in shipped data | Rows | Lane-base nibble |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | QUAD_B | add 1 lane on the RIGHT | near N+1, far N+2 points | unchanged |
| 3 | TRANSITION_A | add 1 lane on the LEFT | near N+1, far N+2 | minus 1 |
| 4 | TRANSITION_B | add 2 lanes (one each side) | near N+1, far N+3 | minus 1 |
| 5 | QUAD_C | drop 1 lane on the RIGHT | near N+1, far N | unchanged |
| 6 | REVERSED_A | drop 1 lane on the LEFT | near N+1, far N | plus 1 |
| 7 | REVERSED_B | drop 2 lanes | near N+1, far N-1 | plus 1 |

Rules read off Keswick (`tg_track_census.py --changes 1`) and confirmed by the
port's LUTs, which were verified against the binary:

* The transition span carries the WIDER lane count in its own nibble. An ADD
  is typed on the span AFTER the seam (its far row is wider than its near
  row); a DROP is typed on the span BEFORE the seam (its far row is narrower).
  Example, Keswick spans 1536..1537: type 7, lanes 4, near 5 points, far 3
  points, then type 1, lanes 2.
* The high nibble of the packed byte is a LANE-BASE offset, not a height (the
  port's `span_height_offset` name is historical). The walker applies
  `sub_lane += h_off - dest_h` across every seam [CONFIRMED @ 0x00444414 in
  the port's `resolve_neighbor`], which is how a lane that disappears on the
  left shifts every remaining lane index by one. Values seen: 5..9, baseline 8.
* Vertex-offset LUTs by type, `k_quad_vertex_offsets` [CONFIRMED @ 0x00474E40]:
  types 3/4 = (-1, 0), types 6/7 = (0, -1), all others (0, 0). AI target LUT
  `k_target_vertex_offsets` [DAT_00473C68]: types 2/3/4 col0 = -1/-1/-2,
  types 5/6/7 col1 = -1/-1/-2. Edge-mask LUTs per type: `s_edge_mask_first/last`
  (`td5_track.c:116`). Heading dispatch classes per type: `td5_track.c:6826`
  (types 3/4 class 1, 6/7 class 2).
* Left/right rail derivation and the collision walker already handle types
  2..7 (they are shipped data); what is untested is the GENERATOR's guardrail
  and pavement emitters on such spans (TG:14854 says so).

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-06 (same branch, after the split): `tg_build_centerline`
draws a lane count per section (knobs `TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_LANE_VARY`, `LANES_MIN`,
`LANES_MAX`, `LANE_PCT`; base `TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_LANES` now 2..8), commits the
change at the section's first node with its side and the lane-base nibble, and
jogs the walk half a lane on one-sided changes (the tangent pass subtracts the
jog). `tg_emit_span_range` sizes each shared row to the narrower span
(`tg_row_points`) and types the wider span 2..7 (`tg_span_type_for`); forks
read their lane count at F and are skipped if the count changes inside their
window. Changes never land on the grid, the last 60 spans, fork windows, bridge
decks or tunnel bores. Proof for seed 20260901: VARY=0 byte-identical to the
pre-lanes build; VARY=1 gives 17 seams, all invariants hold, AI drive clean.
Audit any STRIP.DAT with `python re/tools/tg_strip_audit.py <file>` (exit 1 on a
violation).
The original sketch, kept for the record:

1. `TG_Node.lanes` per node already exists (TG:1876, "1..12"); let the section
   picker assign lane count per section (2..8 in steps of 1 or 2) instead of
   `spec->lanes`.
2. In `tg_emit_strip`, when `lanes(k+1) != lanes(k)`: emit the shared far row
   with `lanes(k+1)+1` points, type the span per the table above, and bump the
   lane-base nibble for left-side changes. Keep `lanes(F) = lanes(F+1) +
   lanes(B0)` at forks (all 147 shipped forks obey it).
3. Route tables (LEFT/RIGHT.TRK) carry a lane per span: renormalize the
   preferred lane across the seam with the same base offset the walker uses.
4. Verify by driving across every transition type with the F12 wireframe and
   the RaceTrace `track` module (sub_lane must stay continuous), then compare
   `airborne_mask` against a Keswick run (handover trap 1).

## 5. Branch types: what shipped forks look like

From the 147 jump records (`AUTOTRACK_TRACK_CENSUS.md`, Branches section):

| Kind | Count | Description |
|---|---|---|
| PARALLEL | 126 | corridor length within 15% of the main distance fork to rejoin: divided carriageway, one-way pair, or a traffic island (37 corridors are 8 spans or shorter) |
| SHORTCUT | 21 | corridor shorter than the main road: the branch is the direct route, the main ring is the scenic one |
| DETOUR | 0 shipped (4 in generated tracks) | corridor longer than the main road: only the generator does this |

Lane split at the fork (`lanes(F) -> lanes(F+1) + lanes(B0)`), by frequency:

* Symmetric: 8 -> 4+4 (40), 6 -> 3+3 (37), 4 -> 2+2 (26). 103 of 147.
* Slip road (corridor narrower): 8 -> 6+2 (9), 7 -> 4+3, 5 -> 3+2, 7 -> 5+2,
  8 -> 5+3, 6 -> 4+2. 20 of 147.
* Main narrower than the corridor: 8 -> 3+5 (8), 8 -> 2+6 (6), 6 -> 2+4,
  7 -> 3+4, 8 -> 1+7, 7 -> 2+5, 5 -> 2+3. 24 of 147.

Every shipped fork rejoins through a type-11 span whose lane count equals the
fork's. Corridor length: min 3, median 32, max 1125 spans (Sydney's single
fork runs 1126 spans, longer than a third of the ring).

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-06 (same branch): `tg_fork_plan` in `td5_tg_branch.c` is a
six-entry ladder rotated by the seed (AVENUE 40 spans sep 0.20, ISLAND 6 spans
sep 0.16, WIDE 120 spans sep 1.0, SLIP 32 spans, MAJOR 60 spans, ISLAND 5
spans); `tg_fork_split_lanes` gives the census lane splits (symmetric, slip
= 1-2 lanes off, major = main keeps 1-2); the fork-aware helpers
`tg_fork_main_shift/wscale` and `tg_fork_br_shift/wscale/lanes_at` feed the strip
rows, the road quads, the gore, the pavement, the clearance query and the
preview from the one per-fork record, so an asymmetric split cannot drift
between them. Knobs `TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_BRANCH_KINDS` (1) and `BRANCH_COUNT` (6).
Not done: true SHORTCUT geometry (a corridor with fewer spans than its main
stretch needs its own centreline and a curved main road inside the fork
window, which the walk currently straightens).

Diagnostic gotcha found while verifying: the race trace's `wall_clear` column
and the HUD's `LANE: lanes=N` line both read the NORMALIZED main span, so on a
car that took a corridor they report the main road's rails and lane count (the
clearance goes negative by exactly the corridor's bow). Check `span_raw >=
ring` before reading either. The AI does take corridors (about 1 fork in 3 in
the drive tests) and follows them. The original list:

1. **Divided carriageway** (parallel, symmetric split, 4..12 wide, 20..60 spans,
   avenue divider already exists): the most common shipped shape and the one
   the handover called "dual lanes" without delivering.
2. **Traffic island / bollard split** (parallel, 3..8 spans, 4 -> 2+2): Paris
   has 14 in a row. Cheap, very visible at city speed.
3. **Slip road** (8 -> 6+2, corridor drifts out then back): the off-ramp look.
4. **Shortcut** (corridor 50..85% of the main distance): the main road takes a
   loop around a block, the corridor cuts through. Needs the corridor to be
   the STRAIGHTER path, so pick it at sweeping curves.
5. **Main-narrower** (8 -> 2+6): swap which side the ring follows so the AI's
   default route is the minor road and the player can take the boulevard.
6. Keep the current detour as a sixth kind, weighted low (it is the one shape
   the shipped tracks never use).

## 6. Diversity backlog beyond lanes and branches

Absent today (zero grep hits in TG unless noted), in priority order by how
often shipped tracks show them:

| Element | Where shipped tracks have it | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Lane-count variation (section 4) | every track | strip emitter surgery, medium |
| Parallel / shortcut / slip-road branch kinds (section 5) | 147 forks | corridor centerline variants, low each |
| Per-span surface variety beyond the biome class (wet patches, cobble strips, the 0xF1..0xFA family with an alternate-surface lane mask other than 0x09) | Keswick 6 codes, TD6 up to 45 | low: `tg_surface_attr` + mask |
| Biome-driven section mix (a city cell wants short straights and 90 deg corners, alpine wants sweepers) | all | low: weight table per biome |
| TD6 art (2226 pages never mined: London brick, Paris stone, Rome ochre, Hong Kong signage, Egypt sand) | 11 levels | manifest + slot reservation per set |
| Elevation extremes: switchback stack, cliff edge with sea below | Bern, Blue Ridge, Switzerland, Tahoe | medium: needs the ACUTE budget and terrain |
| Hairpin at or above 180 deg | Bern, Courmayeur | declared incompatible with the single-axis walk (TG:1980); would need a second progress axis |
| Roundabout | Paris, London (visually) | strip cannot loop; fake as a parallel split around an island mesh |
| Toll booth / gantry rows, railway crossing, stadium, harbour | Washington, Munich, Sydney, Honolulu | scenery only, low each once art is imported |
| Bridge types (arch, truss, suspension) | Sydney, SF, Newcastle | scenery, medium |
| Runtime reuse of shipped MESHES (not just pages) | all | new loader or baked mesh headers, high |

## 7. What was kept intact

* No emitter, knob, default or page slot changed. `MODELS.DAT`, `STRIP.DAT`,
  `TEXTURES.DAT` for a given seed are byte-identical to before this change
  (the generator source did not change).
* Existing headers are not regenerated; `gen_tg_pages.py` refuses to overwrite
  a header unless its manifest says `"regenerate": true`, and refuses pages
  another header already holds.
* The picker change is dev-only, render side, and only touches the label and
  clipboard text.
